lead.headline: Indian and Chinese troops are still facing off at several places along the Arunachal border, the ITBP's chief says
lead.short: Confrontations between Indian and Chinese troops have been taking place at several locations along the Arunachal Pradesh border and are continuing, the director general of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police, Shatrujeet Singh Kapur, said on Thursday. "In the past few days, a situation arose where face-off happened at several locations in Arunachal and it still continues," he said in Alwar.

why.text: It is the first official word that the stand-offs reported since July are real and continuing, after months without comment from the Army or the government.

more: The ITBP guards the 3,488-km Line of Actual Control with China. Kapur said the force is preparing for modern warfare with drones, specialised commandos and new underground shelters, PTI reported.

Reports of a stand-off near Taksing in Upper Subansiri district first emerged in July. An official told The Hindu that troops came face to face near Maja during a routine patrol, and that the People's Liberation Army later returned in larger numbers and pitched tents about 6 to 7 km inside India's perception of the LAC. In August the foreign ministry said peace on the border was of "utmost importance" to relations.

The Congress accused the government on Friday of "suppressing" reports of skirmishes since July, and said Prime Minister Modi was "seen joking around" with Xi Jinping at the BRICS summit in September.

facts.where: several locations in Arunachal, including near Taksing

seconds.headline: Britain takes 32 government services offline as the scramble to patch the PHP flaws spreads, and Japan plans cyberattack drills
seconds.short: Thirty-two British government services were unavailable on Thursday and four more partly so, a minister told the House of Lords, as departments patched the two PHP flaws found with AI help. Websites around the world were taken offline on Wednesday and Thursday. No successful attacks have been reported, but the BBC reports any damage could take months to show.

why.text: Most of the web runs on PHP, so every unpatched site is a door left open, and governments are treating it as an emergency.

more: The tech minister, Baroness Lloyd of Effra, said the outages were "largely" precautionary while updates were applied, and that no large public-facing critical service was affected. The government said its experts are working with OpenAI, whose researchers helped find the first flaw, and international partners.

Olly Whitehouse, chief technology officer of the National Cyber Security Centre, called the event "unprecedented" and said "it will be universally felt". He said there were "no indications" of successful breaches so far, and that advice sent to affected organisations was being acted on.
Japan said it will simulate cyberattacks to test its defences, Reuters reported. PHP's developers released fixes this week and have urged everyone to update at once.

update.new: Britain has 32 services offline and Japan plans drills; no successful attacks reported yet.
update.front: The flaws are now shutting down government services in Britain, and the cyber agency calls it unprecedented.

seconds.headline: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake kills at least 16 people in Tibet's Nagqu region and brings down 339 homes
seconds.short: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Baqên County in Tibet's Nagqu region on Thursday night, killing at least 16 people and injuring 65, 11 of them severely, Chinese state media said. The county lies about 400km north-east of Lhasa. Authorities declared an emergency and sent rescue teams, and more than 12,400 people have been moved from their homes.

why.text: The quake hit a remote, high-altitude area where closed roads make rescue slow, close to India's own Himalayan earthquake belt.

more: Power was cut across the area and 339 homes collapsed, though electricity had been restored in some places by Friday morning, Xinhua reported. Falling rocks have closed roads, making it harder for crews to reach villages high in the mountains.

The US Geological Survey recorded seven tremors near the epicentre, the largest of magnitude 5.2 at a depth of 10km. Shallow quakes do more damage than deep ones. A Nagqu resident, Yixi Cuomu, told Tibet Daily she was asleep when her house began to shake.
China has governed the region, which it calls the Tibet Autonomous Region, since the 1950s.

seconds.headline: OpenAI nears a $30bn funding round at a $1.25tn valuation, led by Coatue and UAE investors, CNBC reports
seconds.short: OpenAI is close to raising up to $30bn of private money at a $1.25 trillion valuation before the new cash, in a round led by Coatue and investors in the UAE, CNBC reported. Terms are still being negotiated. A month ago Bloomberg reported OpenAI was seeking the same sum at $1.4 trillion, so the target has come down.

why.text: At over a trillion dollars OpenAI would be the most valuable private company ever, and the price sets the bar for its own share sale and Anthropic's.

more: CNBC said the UAE money could come with a deal for more computing capacity in the Emirates. OpenAI declined to comment. Its last round, in March, valued the ChatGPT maker at $852bn after the new money, and it filed confidential paperwork for a share sale in June.

The price also bears on Anthropic, the maker of Claude, which is expected to file its public listing documents soon. CNBC reports Anthropic is seeking a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion for its debut. Anthropic raised $65bn at a $965bn valuation in May, in what many expected to be its last private round.

seconds.headline: The Sensex swings 1,100 points from its high as small and mid-sized shares fall for a seventh straight session
seconds.short: Indian shares opened higher on Friday, with the Sensex up 300 points, then slid about 1,100 points from the day's high as smaller companies sold off. By 2pm the Nifty 50 was down 0.6% at about 22,554 and the Sensex 0.4% lower at about 72,964. Broader indices fell up to 3%, a seventh straight session of losses.

why.text: Most Indian investors hold mid and small-cap funds, and a week of falls has wiped lakhs of crores off those holdings.

more: The Economic Times put the day's loss in market value at about ₹10 lakh crore at the low point, when the Nifty dropped below 22,450. Banks fell 1.2%, with Jammu & Kashmir Bank down almost 15% and Karur Vysya, IIFL and Nippon's asset manager down 6% to 7%. Power, capital goods and metals companies each lost about 3%.
IT shares held steady. TCS rose 1.2% and the Nifty IT index has recovered more than 13% in a month. The rupee opened at 94.79 a dollar and weakened to about 94.96.
Oil eased to about $109 a barrel after reaching $112 on Thursday, its highest since 18 May, when the Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia and hits on tankers in the Gulf threatened supply.

facts.broader markets: down up to 3%, seventh straight session

update.new: A sharp intraday swing and a seventh day of falls for small and mid-sized shares.
update.front: Small and mid-sized shares, where most Indian savers sit, have now fallen for seven sessions in a row.

stories.headline: Trump tells Ramaswamy to 'ride with it' as Amy Acton calls his ad featuring her estranged mother 'despicable'
stories.short: Amy Acton, the Democratic candidate for governor of Ohio, called Vivek Ramaswamy's ad featuring her estranged mother "despicable". In it, Donna Arthur says Acton "lied her entire life", but it leaves out that Arthur's husband was charged with raping Acton as a child. Donald Trump defended the ad, telling Ramaswamy at an Iowa rally that "you gotta ride with it".

why.text: Ohio's governor's race on 3 November is one of the midterm contests both parties are watching, and the ad has split Republicans.

more: "Leave it up, and look upstairs and say, 'Thank you God, very much'," Trump said late on Thursday. Earlier he defended Ramaswamy on social media. Vice President JD Vance had told Republicans to stop "whining" about it.

Ohio's outgoing Republican governor, Mike DeWine, who has endorsed Ramaswamy, has reportedly called the ad deeply troubling and asked for it to be taken down. "I've never attacked his family. I would never do that," Acton said at a campaign stop on Wednesday evening, adding that many people have "experienced trauma and abuse in their lives".
Acton and her brother were removed from Arthur's custody after the charge against her husband.

facts.DeWine: reportedly asked for it to be taken down

update.new: Trump backs the ad and Acton calls it despicable.

stories.headline: Barcelona's 19-year-old Xavi Espart is set to start at right-back in Sunday's Clásico, with Koundé not fit to begin
stories.short: Xavi Espart, Barcelona's 19-year-old academy graduate, is expected to keep his place at right-back against Real Madrid at Camp Nou on Sunday, AS reports, after he scored and helped contain Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in the defeat at PSG. Jules Koundé is unlikely to be fit to start. The game kicks off at 01:30 IST on Monday.

why.text: Barcelona lead Madrid by six points, so a win at Camp Nou would leave them nine clear before November.

more: Espart was taken off late in Paris with a knock, but the substitution was a precaution and he is available for what will be his first Clásico. Barcelona lost for the first time this season in that game, and come into Sunday with injuries in defence and questions about their stability at the back.
Madrid will be without Vinícius Júnior, who is suspended, after three wins from three in the Champions League.

Off the pitch, Spain's National Sports Council has filed a formal complaint with the Administrative Tribunal for Sport over La Liga president Javier Tebas. On 16 October Tebas compared Real Madrid TV's methods with the propaganda tactics of Nazi Germany. The 16-page complaint was signed by José Manuel Rodríguez Uribes, the secretary of state for sport.

stories.headline: Verstappen calls Austin's bumps 'unacceptable', as Antonelli arrives with his first mathematical chance of the title
stories.short: Max Verstappen said the bumps at the Circuit of the Americas are "unacceptable" and "out of control" at media day in Austin, and that his joke about needing a new spine was "not really a joke". Kimi Antonelli, 20, arrives for the first time this season with a mathematical chance of winning the championship this weekend.

why.text: If Antonelli wins it he becomes Formula 1's youngest ever champion, in only his second season.

more: Verstappen watched the World Endurance Championship race at the circuit in September and said it looked "extremely badly bumpy". George Russell agreed the track is bumpy but said F1 circuits should be resurfaced every couple of years, because at several tracks the tarmac is "falling apart". "Our ride height's 10mm at the end of the straight," he said, "so any tiny bump you really feel it."

Antonelli admits it is a long shot to settle the title in Texas. Isack Hadjar said Red Bull do not have the fastest car, even after Verstappen won in Malaysia and Singapore, where he finished 7.3 seconds ahead of Charles Leclerc. "If you put Max in the Ferrari, he would have won the race with more margin," Hadjar said.

update.new: Verstappen calls the bumps unacceptable at media day; Russell wants tracks repaved.
